summary: E passes: this is the exact reopen named by CLAIMS.md:73 ('a cheaper dequant'), on a fresh base (1.5008, c63801e7 unchanged). The mechanism is sound and one run is readable, because the arms are interleaved against an in-module DQ0 control. The build must fix the prepare-time budget first: 16 instantiations started at ~181 s can overrun the 300 s prepare limit. It must also take the timing gates against DQ0 and key the decision on pair MODE 0, not on MODE 5.
justification: A, mechanism. Master's dq_stage/dequant8 (submission.py:2673-2741) costs about 15-16 INT ops per k16 step: per bf16x2 SHF + 2 LOP3 + SHL, then HFMA2 against -0. The scale path adds about 7 per step: HADD2.F32 x2, FMUL x2, F2FP pack x2, plus the amortized e4m3 cvt and LDS. A2 cuts the code path to about 10 per word with moe's ext_prop (muse_moe_w4a16/submission.py:5033-5045: 1 + 2 + 2 + ~5). A1 cuts the scale path to about 2 per step (prmt + IMAD), with the broadcast folded into HMUL2 .H0_H0/.H1_H1. So A3 removes roughly 35-40% of the dequant instructions, more than the 24 -> 17-19 the hypothesis claims. Its own census also does not add up: 11 + 4 + 4 = 19, not 17. Exactness holds: e2m1 x e4m3 x 2^-7 has at most 6 significant bits. The judge's scales are clamped to [8, 448] (nvfp4.py:123), i.e. bytes 0x50-0x7E, and even wide_scales stays at >= 0x08, so the [0x08, 0x7E] precondition will hold and A1/A3 will not switch OFF. Evidence for the lever (cb22e610, CLAIMS.md:70-71): t0 - t1 (what dequant adds over MMA-only) is 99 of 294 us at low w13, 157 of 747 at high w13 and 643 of 3570 at ft w13. The overlap levers K-pair, anti-phase and ping-pong all lost (CLAIMS.md:44, 72, 73), which points at per-SMSP contention (ALU pipe / RF ports during RS wgmma) rather than latency. Cutting the dequant's own ALU work attacks that directly. WEAKEST LINK: whether t0 tracks dequant instruction count at all. At high and ft, MODE 2 already sat on the producer floor (t2 = t4 at ft; 356 vs 340 us at high), so a cheaper dequant can only pay there through reduced contention, not a shorter serial dequant. Expect the gain to concentrate at low; high and ft could be flat. Moe's dq2 ran in mma.sync Engine A and at the RS wgmma ladder (LOG:1295, (e) dq2 + RS ~29.8 el/clk/SM vs Engine A ~27); it has never been measured on the rega tile. That is exactly what this run answers. Prior check: experts-rega-producer-scale-expand-all-t (CLAIMS.md:44, 6be2a8d3) moved the same scale work onto producer warps through an extra mbarrier hop and smem ring. This run cuts work on the consumer and adds no barrier or smem, so the difference is real. experts-triton-nvfp4-packed-asm-dequant is a different engine, superseded per CLAIMS.md:39. Not a duplicate. Expected shapes and directions match TASK.md weights and the b2941ea profile: rega is 48-53% of sliding rows; turn_1 is the class with the largest g.
confounders: experts-rega-w13-fast-silu-epilogue and the w2st arm a landing (CLAIMS.md:51, 54, 56): the dq module derives from _rega_fsilu_src(), so master, DQ0 and A1-A3 all carry the same epilogue. They do not confound the arm/DQ0 ratio. They do confound arm/master by the MODE plumbing (anat r2 m0/m was 0.974-1.023, worst at ft cold), which can push a do-nothing arm toward the 0.97 route threshold.
norm-gather + two-phase align (CLAIMS.md:42, 46): they fix the routed inputs and tables (xs/hs from master's own _experts_rega). All arms share them. No confound.
rega engine (CLAIMS.md:41): the dq_stage under test is this engine's. Changing it is the point, not an interaction.
interference: No companion. The diagnostic controls itself: master, DQ0 (master's dequant text in the dq module) and A1/A2/A3 are timed interleaved in the same prepare, on the same inputs, L2 modes and routings. A1 vs A3 isolates the scale path from the code path, and MODE 5 vs MODE 2 vs MODE 0 separates instruction cost from stage time. A gain and a loss are both readable from the per-arm/DQ0 ratios without another check. An ab-revert of fast-silu or w2st would not change what the arms measure. One condition makes this hold: the verdict and the route gate must use arm/DQ0 as well as arm/master. That way a route cannot be credited to the MODE plumbing, which anat r2 showed moves m0/master by up to 2.6%.
rules_flags: None blocking. The A2/A3 permuted bank is a lossless per-word nibble permutation made in prepare (TASK.md:88 allows repacking). Codes stay NVFP4 bits, scales stay E4M3 bytes, and the dequant is bit-identical (gated by torch.equal).

Routed dispatch must stay on prepare flags only (state['rega_dq_ok'][cls]). Add no host sync, print or input-sized allocation to kernel_fn/_experts_rega. The permuted copy must be added to the replay-check key set so state copies stay consistent.

PREPARE TIME (not a rules breach, but a timeout is charged as a failed run, TASK.md:27/110). Master reaches w2st's end at ~180-181 s (cb22e610: 180.0 s; bbca0105: 181.3 s). One 4-instantiation rega build takes 37-40 s. A DQ in {0,1,2,3} x (G, BIG) build is 16 instantiations, likely ~90-140 s, so it ends at ~270-320 s, before any timing. The 205 s rule gates only when nvcc STARTS, and load_inline cannot be interrupted, so this fails the 300 s limit. The build must budget predictively (see open_questions for the concrete requirement).
freshness: E checked. The mechanism's newest claim is CLAIMS.md:73 [refuted] (anti-phase), whose reopen reads 'a cheaper dequant'. This hypothesis is that reopen, using a new mechanism (instruction form) rather than a schedule, so E(i) is met. CLAIMS.md:44 [refuted] covers moving scale expansion onto producer warps, a different mechanism (relocation with an extra barrier hop), and this run stays local to the consumer. CLAIMS.md:68 (register ring), 72 (K-pair) and 73 are schedule changes, not dequant cost. CLAIMS.md:70-71 [lead] supply the evidence. No [landed] claim owns the dequant form (CLAIMS.md:41 is the engine, 51/54/56 are epilogue and near-ties), so E(ii) passes. Board 1.5008 and blob c63801e7 are unchanged since mint (moved 0.00% against a 1.24% margin), so E(iii) passes. user_requested under today's 'run all you want that youre able to' steer: below the bar (EV 0.75%) but allowed.
open_questions: BUILD MUST (prepare budget). Pick one of two. (a) Cut instantiations to fit: DQ in {0, 1, 3} x {w13, w2} at BIG=false only (6 instantiations, low + high classes), with ft skipped and printed SKIPPED. A2 alone is redundant because A3 - A1 gives it. (b) Keep all of them but start the dq build in a background thread at the top of prepare(). The source is static text derived from _rega_fsilu_src(), so nvcc overlaps master's first ~180 s; join it in _rega_dq_phase. Either way, gate the build start predictively: start only if t_now + 1.3 x (fsilu build seconds x n_inst / 4) + 25 s <= 270 s, else print '[rega-dq] OFF: budget'. Print the build seconds and the prepare total.

Use moe's mul_bf16x2_h<H> spelling (mov.b32 {l,l} into fma.rn.bf16x2), not __byte_perm 0x1010/0x3232. Moe's own comment (muse_moe_w4a16/submission.py:5083) says the byte_perm form does NOT fold into HMUL2 .H0_H0/.H1_H1, so it would add an instruction per bf16x2.

Scale layout differs from moe. In rega's record the scale bytes are interleaved per k16 step (byte 2k = row g, byte 2k+1 = row g+8 of sc.x/sc.y; dq_stage's hs[k] -> fs.x/fs.y). So [b_g, 0, b_g8, 0] is a ONE-source prmt of one word (selector from bytes 2k, 2k+1 of sc.x for k<2, sc.y for k>=2), not moe's two-source scale_pair_rt. Keep moe's IMAD form (rt16 m16) so the add stays on the FMA pipe. In rega, dequant8 pairs i=0,2 use sg (H0) and i=1,3 use sg8 (H1) from the same code word, so the A2 permutation is _ea_luts index 2 per pair, applied per 32-bit word of every uint4.

Decision rule. Key lead/landed/refuted on the w13+w2 pair MODE 0 ratio against BOTH DQ0 and master (warm, pop). Use MODE 5 only to attribute the result and to decide the moe/decode hot-half port. As written, branch (1) needs MODE 5 >= 25%, so an arm that routes with a pair cut >= 8% but a MODE 5 cut of 20% would file as [shelf]. A MODE 5 cut < 12% next to a pair cut >= 3% should read as 'contention relief', not 'close'.
Route gate: require arm/master <= 0.97 AND arm/DQ0 <= 0.97 in every round, L2 mode and routing, so the MODE plumbing (anat m0/m 0.974 at ft cold) cannot route a do-nothing arm.

INVALID scope: an arm that is not torch.equal should be OFF for that arm only, with its max|diff| printed. It should not invalidate the whole run. DQ0 fidelity outside 0.97-1.03 should invalidate only that class.

Log tail: anat r2's low-class TIME lines fell outside the 16 KB tail (cb22e610.log starts mid-ft). The <= 3 KB summary printed at once must itself carry the decision numbers per class: per-arm MODE 0/2/5 ratios vs DQ0 and vs master (warm pop, plus cold pop), the PAIR ratio, ROUTE, VERDICT, attrs and SCALES counts. Do not rely on the per-routing TIME lines surviving.

Cheap exhaustiveness check, optional: a one-warp canary that runs dq_stage DQ0 vs each arm over every byte value in each nibble-pair position and every scale byte 0x08-0x7E, compared bitwise, like moe's dq_exact (0 / 121,856, LOG:677). This makes 'exact by construction' a proof rather than coverage over the routings that happen to be sampled.
